complexity.correctness_reason: Lists longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 nodes) make decode/encode raise RecursionError; NeetCode caps list length at 100, so it is safe only under that cap.
complexity.notes: Treating arithmetic as unit cost, decode/encode are single linear passes, but each uses recursion depth equal to the list length, so the recursion stack dominates the O(n) space. The idiomatic approach is an iterative one-pass carry propagation; `encode(a+b) or ListNode(0)` is a slightly cute way to handle the zero case since encode(0) returns None.
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes both linked lists into integers, adds them, then recursively re-encodes the sum into a linked list (with a special case for 0).
